correctness.rationale: Exact Haar correlation identity gives right-invariant Lipschitz bounds for arbitrary metrics; uniform summation yields a positive normalized kernel. Its every irreducible Fourier block is positive definite as weighted sums of positive-semidefinite Fourier correlation matrices, with the underlying Fourier coefficients tending to the identity. Peter–Weyl yields convolution injectivity. The existing connected locally compact continuous-shift theorem and small affine scaling then give the claimed universal one-Lipschitz embedding; the converse is immediate from shift fixed points. Exact finite tests on C5 and S3 verified normalization, nonzero convolution determinant, equivariance and Lipschitz inequalities without substituting finite tests for proof.

originality.rationale: arXiv:2610.13091v1 states the exact fixed-point criterion for connected Lie groups and asks the connected second-countable locally compact case as Problem 1.3; the new claim covers all compact connected metrizable groups, including non-Lie groups. The classical continuous-shift theorem and Peter–Weyl are explicitly used as known inputs. The two earlier Lipschitz papers target Euclidean actions or only Borel embeddings. No equivalent general compact non-Lie topological theorem was found in targeted published searches; an unlocated classical convolution corollary is possible.
residual_risks: The 1974 Jaworski thesis and the 1975 Chen article were not inspected in full; their continuous-target theorem is corroborated by the three inspected primary sources.
An equivalent compact-group positive Fourier smoothing result may occur in older harmonic-analysis literature without the same title, even though no dynamical embedding theorem was located.
This is a self-review only; no external referee has checked the statement.

value.rationale: Provides a full compact-connected branch of explicitly posed Problem 1.3 in arXiv:2610.13091v1, extending beyond finite-dimensional Lie groups to infinite products of circles, compact solenoids and other compact connected metrizable groups. A positive information-preserving convolution filter handles arbitrary compatible right-invariant metrics without Lie derivatives; this is a natural structural extension, not a routine numerical improvement.
